question: Which CAPEC patterns exploit weakness CWE-287, which ATT&CK techniques do they map to, and what mitigations apply?

answer.headline: Gathered 15 record(s) from 2 source(s); 8 cross-source correlation(s) on shared identifiers.
answer.narrative: The CAPEC patterns exploiting CWE-287 are Token Impersonation (CAPEC-633), Adversary in the Middle (AiTM) (CAPEC-94), Upload a Web Shell to a Web Server (CAPEC-650), Utilizing REST's Trust in the System Resource to Obtain Sensitive Data (CAPEC-57), Session Hijacking (CAPEC-593), Authentication Abuse (CAPEC-114), and Authentication Bypass (CAPEC-115). These map to ATT&CK techniques T1134, T1557, T1505.003, T1040, T1185, T1550.001, T1563, and T1548. Mitigations for these techniques include User Account Management (M1018), Privileged Account Management (M1026), Encrypt Sensitive Information (M1041), Disable or Remove Feature or Program (M1042), and Network Segmentation (M1030).

records.name: Token Impersonation
records.label: AttackPattern
records.description: An adversary exploits a weakness in authentication to create an access token (or equivalent) that impersonates a different entity, and then associates a process/thread to that that impersonated token. This action causes a downstream user to make a decision or take action that is based on the assumed identity, and not the response that blocks the adversary.

records.name: Adversary in the Middle (AiTM)
records.label: AttackPattern
records.description: An adversary targets the communication between two components (typically client and server), in order to alter or obtain data from transactions. A general approach entails the adversary placing themself within the communication channel between the two components.

records.name: Upload a Web Shell to a Web Server
records.label: AttackPattern
records.description: By exploiting insufficient permissions, it is possible to upload a web shell to a web server in such a way that it can be executed remotely. This shell can have various capabilities, thereby acting as a "gateway" to the underlying web server. The shell might execute at the higher permission level of the web server, providing the ability the execute malicious code at elevated levels.

records.name: Utilizing REST's Trust in the System Resource to Obtain Sensitive Data
records.label: AttackPattern
records.description: This attack utilizes a REST(REpresentational State Transfer)-style applications' trust in the system resources and environment to obtain sensitive data once SSL is terminated.

records.name: Session Hijacking
records.label: AttackPattern
records.description: This type of attack involves an adversary that exploits weaknesses in an application's use of sessions in performing authentication. The adversary is able to steal or manipulate an active session and use it to gain unathorized access to the application.

records.name: Authentication Abuse
records.label: AttackPattern
records.description: An attacker obtains unauthorized access to an application, service or device either through knowledge of the inherent weaknesses of an authentication mechanism, or by exploiting a flaw in the authentication scheme's implementation. In such an attack an authentication mechanism is functioning but a carefully controlled sequence of events causes the mechanism to grant access to the attacker.

records.name: Authentication Bypass
records.label: AttackPattern
records.description: An attacker gains access to application, service, or device with the privileges of an authorized or privileged user by evading or circumventing an authentication mechanism. The attacker is therefore able to access protected data without authentication ever having taken place.

results.sub_question: What mitigations does ATT&CK list for those mapped techniques?
results.query: MATCH (t) WHERE (t:Technique OR t:SubTechnique) AND t.attack_id IN $ids OPTIONAL MATCH (t)<-[:MITIGATES]-(m:Mitigation) RETURN t.attack_id AS technique_id, t.name AS technique_name, m.attack_id AS mitigation_id, m.name AS mitigation_name LIMIT 300
